text:
maya (PM): quick sync — private deploy roadmap items: egress IP persistence, slim/offline installer, KMS attestation, and launch SLAs. want to align on MVP and next steps.

raj (Eng): agree. egress persistence is the trickiest. operator lifecycle can drop IP handles during major upgrades.

owen (Infra): we can implement a controller that pins egress to a stable handle and rebinds on pod recreation. works for minor upgrades; major operator rewrites remain risky.

noah (Security): telemetry opt-in is non-negotiable for many customers. also KMS integration needs an HSM-compatible contract and clear attestation steps for air-gapped installs.

lina (Solutions): field requests summary: offline signed packages, explicit allowlist CIDRs in installer UI, and an install-only mode with zero outbound requirement.

tess (Eng-Ops): operator-shim idea: shim maintains IP allocations and exposes a small API for heartbeat + bind/unbind. during upgrades it coordinates drain+rebind. prototype should validate <minor-upgrade> flows.

maya (PM): proposed MVP launch criteria: 1) egress IP persistence across minor upgrades (best-effort with documented fallback) 2) offline installer mode with package signing/checksum verification 3) telemetry opt-in + local log export 4) KMS integration contract stub (HSM path) 5) baseline rollback runbook (4-hour target for minor patches). thoughts?

raj (Eng): +1. clarify: persistence is best-effort unless customer opts into operator-shim (higher SLA). shim increases scope but provides determinism.

sophia (Field): customers will accept tiered guarantees if we give explicit SLAs and playbooks. they want a clear failure modal when rebind fails and instructions for network fallback.

owen (Infra): recommend tiered SLAs (standard: best-effort, enterprise: shim + assured minor-upgrade window). 4-hour rollback for major migrations is unrealistic; for minor patches plausible.

noah (Security): for offline installs we need signed bundles, pinned public-key in the installer, and a documented manual attestation flow for legal. add retention requirements for logs.

lina (Solutions): sample installer config customers asked for:
```yaml
installer:
  offline_mode: true
  allowlist_cidrs:
    - 10.0.0.0/8
    - 192.168.0.0/16
  telemetry: opt_in
  signed_bundle: true
```

raj (Eng): action items I see: 1) prototype operator-shim (tess+raj) 2) implement offline-installer flags and signing (raj+owen) 3) KMS/HSM contract draft (noah+lina) 4) SLA tiers + rollback runbook (maya+sophia+owen).

maya (PM): timeline proposal: shim prototype + offline installer POC by end of Q2; KMS contract + SLA baseline by mid-Q3. commit?

tess (Eng-Ops): we can prototype shim in Q2. deliverables: design doc, POC shim, e2e test validating minor upgrade rebind path.

noah (Security): mid-Q3 for KMS draft ok. will loop legal in asap.

lina (Solutions): i'll recruit two pilot customers (one cloud-native, one air-gapped) for field validation.

maya (PM): next steps and deadlines: - raj/tess: shim design PR by 2025-04-18 - raj/owen: offline installer flags + signing PR by 2025-04-25 - noah/lina: KMS requirements draft by 2025-05-02 - maya: SLA baseline and runbook by 2025-05-09.

raj (Eng): will post initial design doc here: https://redwood.team/rfcs/shim-proto — please review.

sophia (Field): :thumbsup: i'll draft the field playbook snippets and pilot checklist.

owen (Infra): perf note: shim adds small control-plane work; expected token-serving delta <2% but we'll measure. will add perf tests to canary.

deploy-bot: jira created: RED-3456 "operator-shim prototype" assigned to raj (Eng)

raj (Eng): thanks — will follow up with a lightweight tech note and link to the test plan.

maya (PM): thanks all. i'll update the roadmap sheet and ping legal. if blockers appear, ping me or drop into #eng-oncall.
